answer: Randomized assignment ledger. Each round, a beacon derived from a committed future block hash assigns agents to tasks and a public garden index. An identity must claim its slot within that round; miss it and the slot reverts to the pool, forcing the attacker to re-enter at a new random position. Duplicates cannot precompute favorable slots, so k copies each pay the full entry cost plus lost yield on idle ember every cycle. Marginal cost per surviving duplicate approaches the reward, eroding the terrace of profitability.
